analysis.investment_thesis: Active Infra is a tiny civil construction contractor (267 Cr mcap) with lumpy revenue that jumped from ₹1 Cr in 2022 to ₹90 Cr in 2025 but just decelerated (-7% YoY). At P/E 26 with decelerating topline and single-digit profit growth, the PEG math doesn't work — the "fast grower" story is already weakening.
key_strengths: Equity base jumped 4x to ₹116 Cr in 2025 (likely IPO/fundraise), cutting D/E sharply
EBITDA margin expanded to 31% in 2025 vs 15% in 2023
ROCE of 15.5% is decent for a contractor, promoter holds a healthy 72.4%
key_risks: Revenue dipped in FY25 (₹97→₹90 Cr) — the growth story already cracking
OCF collapsed from ₹32 Cr to ₹5 Cr in FY25; working capital-heavy EPC model
Micro-cap infra contractor with customer/project concentration and cyclical exposure
red_flags: Revenue deceleration (-7%) while trading at P/E 26 → PEG effectively negative
FY25 OCF ₹5 Cr vs net profit ₹13 Cr — earnings quality deteriorating
3-yr CAGR of 348% is a low-base artifact, not a durable growth rate
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From a Lynch lens, this looks like a recently-listed micro-cap infra contractor where the exciting "growth" chart is really a base-effect illusion — going from ₹1 Cr to ₹89 Cr between FY22 and FY23 tells me FY22 was pre-operations, not that this is a 348% CAGR compounder. The real run-rate is FY23→FY25: revenue flat-to-down (89→97→90) while the market caps it at 26x earnings. That's the opposite of GARP: you're paying a growth multiple for a stalwart-at-best with contractor economics.

The redeeming features are genuine — margins expanded, leverage dropped meaningfully (borrowings 109→60 Cr while equity tripled via fundraise), and ROCE of 15.5% is respectable. But civil construction is a tough, cyclical, working-capital-hungry business where OCF just dropped 85% YoY, and there's no visible niche dominance or moat. I'd want to see either a PEG <1 (requires either ₹110+ price or proof of 25%+ sustained earnings growth) or an order book disclosure showing the FY25 dip is temporary. Until then, HOLD — interesting story, wrong price.
